lines.text: Two small islands in the Gulf of Guinea, empty until the Portuguese came, then built on sugar, cocoa and slavery. This is Sao Tome and Principe.
Portugal found the islands around 1470, and in 1485 the town of Sao Tome was founded, today the capital.
In 1919, on Principe, Arthur Eddington watched a solar eclipse, and showed that Einstein was right about light bending.
In 1936 Miguel Trovoada was born, who would be the first freely elected president.
A year later came Manuel Pinto da Costa, who would lead the islands to independence as their first president.
Fradique de Menezes, born in 1942, would serve as president for a decade.
In 1953 Portuguese forces killed hundreds of islanders in the Batepa massacre, a wound remembered every year.
In 1959 Carlos Vila Nova was born, president since 2021.
And in 1975 Sao Tome and Principe became independent, after five centuries of Portuguese rule.
From plantation islands to a free nation, Sao Tome and Principe found its own voice.
